title: Component contrast playbook and UX decision log
summary: Working playbook and decision log for color/contrast tokens, focus treatment, and screen-reader flows across the Console component library. Purpose: provide deterministic guidance for engineers and designers during handoff and backlog grooming.
goals: Create a repeatable contrast-testing checklist for new and updated components
Propose token mappings for high-contrast and theme variants
Capture UX decisions that affect keyboard and screen-reader interactions
Prioritize backlog items by user impact and implementation complexity
findings: Several form controls use exported tokens that produce WCAG AA failures at small text sizes
Focus rings are inconsistently implemented: some components rely on browser default outline, others use custom box-shadow with insufficient contrast
Icon-only buttons often lack accessible names or aria-label conventions
Live region announcements are missing for asynchronous actions (save, deploy, model fallback) in several screens
proposed_actions: Audit: run automated contrast check across all component tokens at 12px and 16px and report failing pairs (owner: eng-design-team)
Token mapping: create explicit tokens for emphasis/low-emphasis/background/interactive states with proposed hex values and relative token names
Keyboard: standardize focus treatment component-level -- include tokens for focus-color, focus-offset, focus-width
A11y fixes: add aria-labels to icon-only buttons; implement polite live regions for non-blocking status messages
Testing: add a lightweight visual regression step for focus/contrast states in Storybook CI
wireframe_notes: For the rollout modal: add visible focus trap outline and 'Escape' hint in footer
Model-selection list: include role=listbox and aria-activedescendant updates during keyboard nav
Dedicated capacity card: show low-contrast badge only in low-emphasis token; ensure text over badge meets AA when badge present
Settings page toggle: use large touch target (44px) and ensure state change is announced
accessibility_issues: WCAG contrast failures on secondary buttons at 12px (fail AA)
Screen reader text order differs from visual order on deployment pipeline page
Color-dependent status indicators without redundant text or icons
decisions: Adopt token naming convention: ds-token--role--state (example: ds-token--interactive--hover)
Primary focus ring: 3px solid token-focus-primary with offset 4px; soft-shadow fallback for browsers that clip outline
High-contrast theme: toggle enabled in user prefs and respected by console-level CSS variables
Icon buttons will require either visible label or aria-label attribute enforced by lint rule
open_questions: Should we support user-scalable color themes beyond high-contrast (e.g., protanopia optimized)?
How aggressively should we migrate legacy components vs. wrap them with accessibility wrappers?
Is automated Storybook scanning sufficient vs. manual testing for edge cases?
implementation_notes: Prefer CSS variables for token surface so Dedicated/Private deployments can theme at root
Provide fallback tokens for older browsers; use computed contrast checks in Storybook snapshots
Pair engineers with design reviewer for each PR touching tokens
references: A11Y Color Contrast Calculator - internal tool
